deities: Goddess Yamuna (worshipped at the adjacent Yamunotri Temple)

history.summary: NON-TEMPLE: KEEP-OR-DROP DECISION NEEDED — Divya Shila is a sacred reddish-brown rock pillar near the Surya Kund hot springs at Yamunotri, not a temple building, like seq 2237 (Vandiyur Mariamman Teppakulam, sacred tank precedent). Pilgrims worship the Shila before entering the Yamunotri Temple, and according to the Skanda Purana touching it grants spiritual liberation. It is an integral part of the Yamunotri pilgrimage ritual rather than a standalone shrine. CSV town 'Yamunotri' retained; actual district is Uttarkashi (Uttarakhand).

name: Divya Shila
town_description: Yamunotri is the mountain pilgrimage site at the source of the Yamuna River in Uttarkashi district, sitting at about 3,293 m beneath the Bandarpunch peak. Reached by a 6 km trek from Janki Chatti, it is the traditional starting point of the Char Dham Yatra, known for its hot springs, the Divya Shila and the Champasar Glacier further uphill.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaktism — sacred rock pillar worshipped before entering the Yamunotri Temple)

travel.airport: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun, about 200 km
travel.railway: Dehradun or Rishikesh railway stations, then road to Janki Chatti
travel.road: Road up to Janki Chatti (via Dehradun-Barkot); then a 6 km trek to Yamunotri and the adjacent Surya Kund

visitor_information.best_time: May to mid-June and mid-September to October, within the Yamunotri open season
visitor_information.opening_hours: Accessible during Yamunotri Temple darshan hours, 6:00 AM - 8:00 PM in season
